conflict.note: the evaluator declared these three fields and then refused to compare them, which is why the stored baseline shows no verdict for them

explanation.cause: two independent producers write the same field names for the same shape and are never reconciled

producerA.name: region
producerA.semantics: parameters of a clipped scanline fill

producerB.name: plan
producerB.semantics: parameters of the technique the planner believes the shape needs, satin included

explanation.whyNotReconciled: no stage merges plan back into regions. exportPipeline.js does not import stitchPlanner, and buildFinalCommands never receives ctx.stitchPlan. The only merge path is manual: the user pressing Apply in StitchPlannerPanel (src/pages/Editor.jsx onApplyPlan), which writes stitch_type, angle and underlay onto the regions.
explanation.consequence: for the same shape, region.density = 0 while plan density = 0.4; the two numbers describe different techniques and cannot be compared as if they were one quantity

resolutionForP1.decision: region is the authoritative producer for evaluation and for any future rule
reasoning: region.stitch_type is the value every command consumer actually reads (buildFinalCommands, canvas, Final Look, export)
plan is advisory and unreachable from the command path without manual user action, so treating it as authoritative would evaluate something the machine never sews
the baseline already selected regions as its region source (pipelineSnapshot.json → selectedRegionSource = 'regions'); keeping that choice preserves comparability with BASE-ENGINE-A-WIDTHS-V1
resolutionForP1.planRole: kept as a declared, separate observation — never merged silently, never used to fill an unavailable field
resolutionForP1.appliesTo: evaluation and P1 rule design only; no productive code was changed by this decision

fieldSourceRule.planFields: recorded under an explicit plan namespace when present, and reported as a separate observation
fieldSourceRule.forbidden: substituting a plan value for a missing region value, or averaging the two
